newsitem.title: CANADA: Transport ministers seek Canada grain delay probe.
newsitem.headline: Transport ministers seek Canada grain delay probe.

text.p: Transport ministers of British Columbia, Saskatchewan and Manitoba Tuesday called for a federal inquiry into delayed grain shipments to Pacific ports.

"The (Provincial) Ministers met this morning via conference call and agreed to call upon the federal government to direct the Canadian Transportation Agency to hold an inquiry into the backlog in grain movements, as authorized under Section 49 of the Canada Transportation Act," the Saskatchewan government said in a release.
Heavy snow, extreme cold and equipment failure led to delays in rail shipments to Pacific ports since early January.
The Canadian Wheat Board faces more than C$15 million in demurrage fines, and admitted to deferring sales.

"The backlog in the grain handling and transportation system is costing Prairie producers an estimated C$65 million in lost revenues," Saskatchewan Transportation Minister Andy Renaud said in the statement.
Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said Monday he spoke to the presidents of Canadian National Railway and CP Rail System about speeding up grain movement.

"We are calling upon David Anderson, federal minister of transport, to get to the bottom of this issue. It is imperative that the real causes of this failure in the system are identified and addressed so that similar crises are avoided in the future," Saskatchewan's Renaud said.
Japan said a month ago it may seek wheat elsewhere.

The Saskatchewan transportation ministry estimated that Western Canada's gross domestic product could lose C$125 million due to deferred sales, demurrage fees reducing the CWB pool accounts, additional road damage due to increased trucking, and other costs.
Thirty five ships waited to load grains and oilseeds at Canada's Pacific ports on Monday with one ship waiting as long as 45 days, CWB spokeswoman Rhea Yates said.
There were 3,433 grain and oilseed railcars unloaded in Vancouver in the week ended March 9 compared to a target of 3,400, Yates said.
Prince Rupert railcar unloads, however, totalled 1,299 hopper cars compared to a weekly target of 1,500, Yates said.
